 Memorial Day 2026 dropped MagSafe power banks to their lowest prices of the year, and every keeper in the lineup is now Qi2 or Qi2.2 certified, starting at $16.99 and topping out around $90. Prices below verified against retailer and brand pages on May 25. This year’s MagSafe banks ship with proper certification, higher wattage, and Memorial Day discounts deep enough to make uncertified knockoffs pointless. Whether you need a slim daily carry pack or a 10,000mAh Qi2.2 25W bank that charges nearly as fast as a wired adapter, the 2026 lineup has options that actually stick and charge fast.
 Two specs separate the keepers from the junk drawer this year. Qi2 versus Qi2.2 sets the wireless ceiling at 15W or 25W, and certified magnetic alignment is the difference between a bank that locks on for a full top-off and a knockoff that slips and quietly drops to the 7.5W Qi cap. Price per mAh, pocketability, and pass-through wired output round out the ranking.
 Below are seven banks worth your money right now, ordered from cheapest to most expensive so you can buy as much capacity and speed as your budget actually needs. No uncertified gimmicks, no 5W relics with a magnet glued on.

 1. Energizer 5,000mAh Slim Metal Qi2 MagSafe Power Bank
 Energizer’s slim metal 5K is the cheapest certified Qi2 bank on the list and proof you don’t need to spend $40 to get a magnet that actually locks. It’s a 5,000mAh pack with a metal shell, Qi2-certified magnetic alignment, 15W wireless and a 20W USB-C output, an LED battery display, and a second output for charging two devices at once. Capacity is the trade-off. A 5,000mAh cell tops up an iPhone 17 about once, not multiple times. At $16.99 from $29.99 during Best Buy’s Memorial Day deal, it’s the budget pick if you only need to keep your phone alive until you find a wall outlet.
 Price : $15.99
 Where to Buy : Best Buy 
 2. LISEN Ultra Slim 5,000mAh Qi2 15W MagSafe Power Bank
 LISEN’s pocket-friendly EDC pick trades capacity for thinness. At 0.38 inches thick, the Ultra Slim 5K actually drops into jeans without sticking out, and it locks to a MagSafe iPhone with Qi2-certified alignment instead of magnetic guesswork. The 5,000mAh cell delivers roughly a 60 to 80 percent top-up on an iPhone 17 after real-world capacity loss, with 7.5W to the iPhone over MagSafe and a 20W USB-C port for faster wired top-offs. At $39.99, it’s the cheapest certified Qi2 EDC pick on this list.
 Price: $19.99
 Where to Buy : Amazon 
 3. Mophie Qi2 Powerstation 10K
 Mophie’s Qi2 Powerstation 10K is the brand-name 10K pick that doesn’t make you bet on an unknown label. It’s a 10,000mAh Qi2-certified bank with a 15W magnetic charging surface, a 30W USB-C PD port, and LED indicator lights to check remaining battery at a glance. Mophie has been shipping MagSafe-compatible power banks since the standard was Apple-only, and the Qi2 certification here means the magnet locks instead of slipping. At $49.99 from $64.99 at Best Buy, it’s the pick if you’d rather buy a Qi2 10K from a name with two decades of brand experience and a 2-year warranty behind it.
 Price: $52.19
 Where to Buy : Amazon 
 4. Sharge ICEMAG 2 Qi2 15W 10,000mAh Power Bank
 Sharge’s first active-cooling Qi2 bank is still the best-value pick in the brand’s lineup. The ICEMAG 2 packs 10,000mAh into a transparent shell with a built-in fan that keeps the magnetic pad cool during long sessions, 30W max two-way USB-C, a foldable kickstand, and dynamic RGB if that’s your thing. The Qi2 15W ceiling matches the LISEN, Mophie, and Anker picks, but the cooling module is what lets it charge longer without thermal throttling. It earns its spot at $52.90, down from $69.90, for anyone who tops off through a full workday.
 Price: $69.90

 5. Baseus PicoGo AM52 Qi2.2 25W 10,000mAh Power Bank
 The PicoGo AM52 is where wireless stops being the slow option. It’s a Qi2.2 25W bank that pushes around 30 percent faster wireless than 15W MagSafe, and a triple cooling system keeps the magnetic pad from throttling under sustained 25W loads. The 10,000mAh capacity is here, plus 45W USB-C wired (the highest wired output on this list), an integrated USB-C cable, and simultaneous two-device charging. Macworld calls it the slimmest 25W 10,000mAh power bank they’ve tested, with fast 45W wired and 25W wireless outputs, and WIRED features it as their Qi2 25W built-in-cable pick. At $59.99 from $79.99 direct from Baseus, it’s the best-value Qi2.2 pick on this list.
 Price: From $55.98

 6. Anker MagGo Power Bank Slim 10K, Qi2 15W
 Anker’s MagGo Slim 10K is the brand-name pick if you want Anker’s reliability and warranty support behind the magnet. At 0.58 inches thick, it’s a 10,000mAh Qi2-certified bank that pushes 15W wireless and 30W wired USB-C. Aerogel thermal insulation keeps the charging surface cool under load, which matters during sustained top-offs in a pocket. Anker rates it for iPhone 12 through 15 series with full 15W magnetic fast charging, and it also charges iPhone 16 and 17 wirelessly via Qi2. Direct from Anker it’s $79.86 right now, the lowest the Slim 10K has hit this spring.
 Price: $49.99
 Where to Buy : Amazon 
 7. UGREEN MagFlow Qi2.2 25W 10,000mAh MagSafe Power Bank
 UGREEN’s MagFlow is the premium pick if you want maximum grip and three charging methods from one device. It’s a 10,000mAh Qi2.2-certified MagSafe pack built around an array of 17 N52 magnets, the strongest magnetic hold on this list, with 9N gripping force that keeps the bank from slipping mid-pocket. Qi2.2 25W wireless is here, plus a 30W nylon-braided USB-C cable built into the bank that doubles as a carry strap, and a separate 30W USB-C port for a third device. A smart digital display shows real-time charge level and wattage. Direct from UGREEN it’s $89.99, with a 33-percent-off code that drops it to about $60.
 Price: $54.98 (On Sale from $89.99)
 Where to Buy : Amazon 
 Memorial Day 2026 MagSafe Power Bank Deals
 Five of the seven picks above are on Memorial Day discount through May 25:
 Energizer Slim Metal 5K : $15.59
 Mophie Qi2 Powerstation 10K : $49.99
 Sharge ICEMAG 2 : $69.90

 UGREEN MagFlow Qi2.2 25W : $54.98
 The LISEN Ultra Slim 5K and Anker MagGo Slim 10K are at regular price right now, with the Anker Slim 10K matching the same $79.86 at  Anker direct.
 How to Pick the Right MagSafe Power Bank in 2026
 Four questions cover most carry scenarios. Do you need Qi2 15W or Qi2.2 25W? If you top off overnight or while scrolling, 15W is fine and the cheaper picks here cover you. If wireless is your primary charging method, only the Baseus PicoGo AM52 and UGREEN MagFlow keep pace with wired speeds. One caveat: Qi2.2’s 25W ceiling only applies to iPhone 16 and 17 series running iOS 26. iPhone 12 through 15 still tops out at 15W even with a Qi2.2 bank, so the cheaper Qi2 picks are the smarter buy on those phones.
 How slim does it need to go? The Energizer Slim Metal 5K, LISEN Ultra Slim 5K, and Baseus PicoGo AM52 are the only banks here that genuinely disappear into a front pocket. Want a built-in cable? The Baseus PicoGo AM52 and UGREEN MagFlow integrate USB-C right on the bank, so you skip the dongle hunt every time you charge a second device.
 Last question, certified or uncertified? Skip anything that doesn’t say Qi2 or Qi2.2 on the spec sheet. Uncertified magnetic banks slip, run hot, and quietly drop to the 7.5W Qi cap on iPhone 12 and later, which makes them slower than a $10 USB-C cable from a gas station. The seven above all pass that bar. Pick the one that matches your wattage ceiling and pocket budget.
 Frequently Asked Questions
 Are Qi2.2 MagSafe power banks worth it over Qi2?
 Yes, if wireless is your primary charging method. Qi2.2 jumps the wireless cap from 15W to 25W, which actually exceeds Apple’s standard 20W USB-C iPhone charger . If you mostly top off overnight or while scrolling, Qi2 15W is plenty and saves you $15 to $30. 
 What’s the difference between certified and uncertified MagSafe power banks?
 Certified Qi2 or Qi2.2 banks include the magnet array and alignment specs that lock the bank to your iPhone for full-speed charging. Uncertified magnetic banks use weaker generic magnets that slip out of position and quietly drop to the 7.5W Qi cap on iPhone 12 and later, which makes them slower than a basic wired charger. 
 Can a 10,000mAh MagSafe power bank charge a MacBook?
 Only at slow speeds with the picks on this list. The highest USB-C output here is the Baseus PicoGo AM52 at 45W, which powers a MacBook Air at its standard charging rate but won’t trigger Apple’s fast-charge mode (that needs 70W or more). For real laptop fast-charging on the go, look at dedicated laptop-class power banks rated 65W or higher, those are heavier and typically run $100 and up. 
 Are MagSafe power banks safe to bring on a plane?
 Yes. All seven picks here are 10,000mAh or smaller, which puts them under the 100Wh TSA and FAA carry-on limit (a 10,000mAh bank is roughly 37Wh). You must carry them in cabin baggage rather than checked luggage. Confirm the watt-hour rating printed on the bank before travel.

 I still own power banks that I struggle to grip in one hand. Such items lurk in the bottom of a cupboard awaiting only the end of days rather than a long train journey or city break vacation.
 Batteries have been getting smaller for years, but recent advances have slimmed phone power banks to shirt-pocket size.
 Solid-state electrolytes are replacing flammable liquid electrolytes with more stable, efficient materials that allow for smaller, more compact, and safer battery designs. While we haven’t tested any fully solid-state power banks, we have been seeing semi-solid-state cells where flammable liquid is reduced to a fraction of that found in standard lithium-ion batteries.
 It’s not all about size—these batteries are safer and should last significantly longer with a greater number of cycles before the battery degrades.
 BMX
 Size matters: How thin is it compared to other Qi2 power banks?
 But size does matter when you’re carrying the power bank in your pocket or backpack.
 BMX, not the little trick bicycle ridden by kids and hipsters but a company called Better Mobile Xperience, has just released a new magnetic wireless power bank that it claims is the “world’s thinnest” 5,000mAh Qi2 power bank.
 The SolidSafe Air 5K doesn’t stray far from the usual length and width of today’s magnetic wireless power banks (4.1 x 2.8 inches / 103 x 70mm), but when it comes to depth (or height, however you look at it) it is truly tiny at just 0.27 inches (6.8mm).
 In comparison, the iPhone Air is only slightly thinner at 5.6mm, with a 3149mAh (12.4Wh) battery capacity.
 While we haven’t tested every single wireless power bank model that exists, we pride ourselves in checking out all those from our most trusted power brands, including Anker, Ugreen, Belkin, EcoFlow, Baseus, Kuxiu, ESR, Zens, Statik and more.
 The margin might be coming down in size, but the SolidSafe Air 5K does indeed live up to BMX’s claim, although the Baseus Picogo Air Magnetic Power Bank (AM71) matches it on slimness if not quite on performance (82% vs 89%).
 The closest we have measured in terms of slimness are:
 BMX SolidSafe Air 5K : 6.8mm
 Baseus Picogo Air (AM71) : 6.8mm
 Anker Nano 5K MagGo Slim : 8.6mm
 Vonmählen Evergreen Mag 5000mAh : 8.6mm
 PhoneSuit Elite Mag Slim 5K : 8.9mm
 Baseus PicoGo Ultra-Slim 5K : 8.9mm
 Kuxiu S2 5K (also semi-solid state): 10mm
 Infinacore M3 Mini 5K : 10.6mm
 Clearly, the SolidSafe Air is the thinnest 5K magnetic wireless power bank that we have tested, alongside the non-solid-state Baseus AM71.
 Simon Jary
 Weight matters too
 What about its weight? When it’s on your person or in the bag you are carrying, weight is as important as size; if not more. The SolidSafe Air weighs 4.1oz (116g); to compare, the iPhone Air weighs 165g.
 Let’s compare that to our other slim power banks mentioned above.
 BMX SolidSafe Air 5K : 4.1oz (116g)
 Baseus Picogo Air (AM71) : 3.7oz (105g)
 Anker Nano 5K MagGo Slim : 4.3oz (122g)
 Vonmählen Evergreen Mag 5000mAh : 4.34oz (123g)
 PhoneSuit Elite Mag Slim 5K : 3.88oz (110g)
 Baseus PicoGo Ultra-Slim 5K : 3.77oz (107g)
 Kuxiu S2 5K (also semi-solid state): 6.14oz (174g)
 Infinacore M3 Mini 5K : 3.88oz (110g)
 The SolidSafe Air is therefore not the lightest power bank we’ve tested. That honor goes to the Baseus PicoGo Air.
 However, we don’t think 0.4oz or 11g is going to be noticeable by anything other than a set of precision scales.
 BMX
 Design: Does the slim design affect battery life or charging speed?
 The SolidSafe Air is so thin that the magnetic coil must be raised a little from the otherwise flat surface of the power bank.
 Looking at the distance between the USB-C charging port and the sides makes me think it will be nearly impossible to get any thinner—but, fear not, someone will.
 Gold, Black, and Silver were the first SolidSafe Air 5K portable chargers released. BMX
 It’s now available in a choice of five colors: Gold, Black, Silver, Burgundy, and Glacier. That covers all the equally thin iPhone Air and now iPhone 18 Pro models with the latest Glacier and Burgundy colors.
 BMX has now added Burgundy and Glacier colors to match more iPhones, including the iPhone 18 Pro models. BMX
 The battery indicator is the standard set of four LEDs to let you know how much power is left in the power bank’s battery. One of the thinnest power banks we’ve reviewed is the PhoneSuit Elite Mag Slim 5K , and this boasts a digital percentage display, which is far more accurate, but such display on a 5K power bank is are, and to its credit, the SolidSafe Air’s LEDs are brighter than most.
 The SolidSafe Air is reinforced with titanium to make it more durable against impact. That combined with the safer semi-solid electrolytes should make the power bank inherently safer than most power banks.
 Semi-solid-state cell technology reducing flammable liquid content improves thermal stability and lowers fire risk compared to conventional lithium-ion batteries. It should also mean the SolidSafe Air can be charged, discharged and recharged many more times than a traditional lithium-ion power bank.
 Performance also matters
 The 5000mAh (milliamp hour) battery is rated at 18.5Wh (watt hours). This is the sweet spot for a power bank that is lightweight and slim but still has enough capacity to offer a decent iPhone recharge. Remember the iPhone Air’s battery capacity is 3149mAh (12.4Wh). The closer match is the iPhone 17 Pro Max’s 5088mAh (20Wh) battery. Find out your iPhone’s battery capacity in our long list.
 We test power banks by running down an iPhone 16 Pro to 0% and seeing to what percentage the power bank can take the phone’s battery. In this test the BMX SolidSafe Air 5K achieved an impressive score of 89%, among the highest of all the magnetic wireless power banks we have had in the Macworld Labs.
 Simon Jary
 The SolidSafe Air employs the Qi2 magnetic charging technology, so can supply up to 15W of power wirelessly.
 Some larger 10K power banks—such as the Kuxiu K1 , Baseus PicoGo 25W 10K , Ugreen MagFlow and Sharge Icemag 3 —use the newer Qi2.2 tech that can handle 25W for compatible iPhones (iPhone 16 and later). 25W should charge an iPhone (16 or later) from 0-50% in around half an hour, while 15W takes about 45 minutes. We are still waiting for a 5K power bank that is as fast as 25W.
 Use the charging port with a cable (USB-C to USB-C for iPhone 15 and later, USB-C to Lightning for older iPhones) to gain a little faster 20W of power. A neat function is simultaneous wired (using a cable in the power bank’s charging port) and wireless charging. Via this method you get 10W wired plus 12W wireless for 22W power—not so far off the 25W that Qi2.2 would have supplied.
 The power bank itself is charged at up to 15W, which is quite slow in comparison to others that have input speeds of between 18-30W. if charging overnight or not in a hurry, this shouldn’t matter. A full recharge of the power bank should take around 2 hours.
 Price
 The SolidSafe Air 5K Solid-State Qi2 Power Bank is available on the BMX website for $59.99 , with Amazon sales starting at the end of March.
 For alternatives check our reviews of the best magnetic wireless power banks .
 Should you buy the BMX SolidSafe Air 5K Solid-State Qi2 Power Bank
 The titanium SolidSafe Air is wafer-thin and can slip into a shirt pocket without worrying the stitching. You can charge your iPhone (12 and later) wirelessly at 15W or 22W when using both wired and wireless outputs, which is fast. There are power banks that recharge themselves faster, and power banks with smarter battery displays, but the BMX SolidSafe Air is the slimmest semi-solid-state 5K Qi2 power bank you can buy—indeed, in our experience, it’s both one of the slimmest and lightest magnetic wireless power banks on the market.

 Best high-capacity 10k MagSafe power banks 
 Best small portable 5K magnetic power banks 
 Best multi-device charging MagSafe power banks 
 Best capacity magnetic power bank for you
 You should consider size when it comes to a power bank: physical size and battery capacity. The higher the battery capacity, the more recharging power you’ll get from the power bank—but you’ll also be carrying around a larger, heavier item. Lighter, slimmer power banks are easier to pocket even when clamped to your phone. Larger power banks might not fit in your trouser pocket and can slide off easier when pocketed even if clamped magnetically.
 10K power banks (with a 10000mAh battery capacity) can charge a phone close to two times over, while 5K (5000mAh) battery packs usually stretch between 60-75%, which is often enough to get you to the next wall-socket powering opportunity. If you are relying on the power bank for long-haul travel or a camping trip, a 10K battery or higher will suit you better. Belkin even offers a mid-range 8K power bank.
 Milliamp hours ( mAh ) is quite a blunt measurement of battery capacity. It’s great for quickly differentiating between power bank sizes but we also list the capacity in the more accurate watt hours ( Wh ).

Qi2 25W brings wireless charging close to wired speed but only iPhones 16 and later support that speed, and some power banks include a built-in USB-C cable for even faster charging up to 45W. The iPhone Air can manage 20W max on even a 25W charger. See Which wireless tech is best for your iPhone? .

In our tests, it was very close in battery charging power to the top scorers—charging an iPhone 16 Pro nearly twice over. This version isn’t available in the Pro’s bright orange color.
 The first version of SmartCharge Gen 1 has one USB-C for iPhone 15/16/17/18 and a Lightning cable for older iPhones. if that suits you better, Amazon still has stock at the time of writing.
 Dominik Tomaszewski / Foundry
 Another plug-in-the-wall power bank option is the Infinacore P3 Pro , pictured above, which costs $129 / £102, and can charge four devices at the same time, including an iPhone at 15W Qi2. It lacks the integrated USB-C cable found on the Statik power bank but as it plugs directly into a wall power socket you won’t need to carry a cable to recharge the power bank itself. Like the Statik battery pack, it comes with U.K., E.U, and AU/NZ travel adapter plug heads. As well as the Qi2 charging pad, there are two USB-C ports and one USB-A. The P3 Pro also boasts an excellent display, showing charging speed, battery status, temperature, and charge time remaining. 
 Read our full 
 Statik SmartCharge Pro review 
 If you don’t need a portable power bank, check out the best MagSafe chargers that we have tested. Also check out our tests of the best iPhone chargers for wired charging solutions, and of course to refill your iPhone power bank. 
 How we tested
 MagSafe charger testing was conducted using an iPhone 13 Pro, iPhone 15 Pro and 16 Pro, subscribed to a 5G network and WiFi, with screen off and all default settings.
 Our test is a simple battery recharge shootout. We let our test-unit iPhone Pro (3095mAh battery capacity) drain to just 10% and then set the Battery Pack to work recharging the phone. We then assigned the charger a score of whatever percentage it managed to charge the iPhone to and subtract the 10%; we test each model at least twice.
 It’s not a real-world test of day-to-day use where you’ll likely be using your phone for various tasks (of varying battery usage) and in different environmental conditions and network configurations. But it does give us a common score format that we can use to compare different battery-pack models.
 Why is magnetic wireless better?
 The MagSafe connection to Apple’s iPhone is precise enough to make wireless charging more efficient as around 20% of non-magnetic power loss is from poor placement of a phone and the wireless charging pad. Standard Qi wireless charging can lose as much as 50% of the portable battery’s power, but MagSafe and Qi2 wireless charging loses ‘just’ 30%. Hot out of the gadget laboratory, the new Qi 2.2 (also known as Qi2 25W) brings even faster 25W wireless charging for the iPhone 16, 17 and 18. 15% will be plenty fast enough for most of us but who doesn’t want the fastest possible charging when your iPhone’s battery icon is in the red?
 Why comparing Watt Hours is better than Milliamp Hours
 Phone batteries are generally rated in Milliamp Hours (mAh) but this is a measure of electrical charge, while a Watt Hour is equal to one watt of energy consumed for one hour of time.
 When comparing battery capacities and how much a power pack will boost a phone’s internal battery, energy is more important than electrical charge.
 And mAh ignores a battery voltage, which determines the wattage (power) of a battery.
 If the mAh is the same, the higher the voltage, the greater the actual stored power.
 For example, Apple’s MagSafe Battery Pack is rated at just 1460mAh but it has a higher voltage potential (7.62V) than the iPhone (3.81V) or other battery packs, meaning that it can provide more power to an iPhone than its mAh suggests; in fact, it is actually 2920mAh.
 To go into further depth about this read our feature iPhone battery capacities compared that also lists all iPhones battery life in mAh and Wh.
 Anatomy of a magnetic power bank
 TORRAS
 A lot more than a battery goes into the making of a magnetic power bank.
 Of course, the battery is the most important component, but the wireless charging coils and magnetic connection are vital for efficient and therefore fast and powerful charging. The transmitter coil transfers power by electromagnetic induction.
 The magnets need to be set up to exactly connect the transmitting coils—here on the power bank— to the receiving coils, in this case inside the iPhone.
 The example shown above is the Torras MagStall Wireless Power Bank, reviewed in our chart. You can see the various parts, including that power bank’s rotating stand/handle.
 Which magnetic wireless tech is right for each iPhone?
 iPhone 7 and earlier: Don’t support wireless charging. 
 iPhone 8 – iPhone X/XS/XR: Support wireless charging. iPhone 8 and later can charge wirelessly at 7.5W but on a less efficient non-magnetic Qi pad.
 iPhone 11 and earlier: Don’t support MagSafe. iPhone 8 and later can charge wirelessly but on a less efficient non-magnetic Qi pad.
 iPhone 12 – iPhone 15: Support MagSafe and Qi2. Can wirelessly charge at 7.5W with “MagSafe-Compatible” power banks and chargers, and at 15W with certified MagSafe or Qi2 power banks and chargers.
 iPhone 16 – iPhone 18: Support MagSafe, Qi2 and Qi2.2. Can wirelessly charge at 7.5W with “MagSafe-Compatible” power banks and chargers, at 15W with certified MagSafe or Qi2 power banks and chargers, and at 25W with Qi2.2-certified power banks and chargers.
 Is charging via a cable faster or safer than magnetic wireless charging?
 Charging via a cable is nearly always faster than wireless, even the latest Qi2.2 wireless chargers. Wireless charging is inefficient, losing some of its energy transfer through heat, for example. MagSafe, Qi2, and Qi2.2 magnetic connections dramatically improve efficiency but sticking a cable in is still a faster method, if not as convenient.
 Most magnetic wireless power banks include at least one USB-C port, and some even include a port and an integrated cable for ultimate convenience. Models after the iPhone 17 can charge to 50% in 20 minutes or under via a cable and a 45W or higher charger or power bank. But wireless is so simple and cable-free that we don’t mind waiting an extra 15 minutes or so to reach such a charge wirelessly.
 Why does my phone occasionally charge slowly or even stop charging?
 This phone charging behavior is due to the built-in battery management feature on your iPhone. A phone heats up during charging as power is exchanged between the charger’s coils and the iPhone’s own. The phone actively adjust its charging behavior accordingly. This can slow down or temporarily pause charging to protect battery health and extend its lifespan. This is completely normal. Once the phone cools down, charging will automatically resume as normal.
 What is a semi solid state battery?
 The material that carries ions back and forth inside a battery is called “electrolyte”. Traditional lithium-ion batteries use a volatile, free-flowing liquid for electrolyte. As their name suggests, solid-state batteries use a solid material such as a ceramic or polymer. But semi-solid-state batteries are more common in today’s new generation of power banks.
 A semi-solid-state battery uses a mix of solid particles in a much smaller amount of liquid, making a hybrid thick gel, paste or slurry. By reducing the liquid content to a minimum, semi-solid-state batteries increase stability and durability and significantly lower the risk of leaks, fires, and dangerous thermal runaway.
 What about non-wireless power banks?
 Wireless charging—especially magnetic wireless charging—is super convenient and does away with the need to carry around messy cables to connect your device to the battery pack.
 But wired charging is nearly always faster and not much of an inconvenience if you are not out and about. Over on our sister site Tech Advisor I have reviewed the best power banks that includes standard non-wireless battery packs that might be a decent solution as well as the power banks reviewed above.
 Do magnetic power banks work when the iPhone is in a case?
 Yes, most quality iPhone cases are compatible with MagSafe having their own magnet ring to ensure a close connection between the power bank’s magnetic charging coils and the iPhone’s own. You can find exactly which are supported in our roundups of the best iPhone 17 cases , best iPhone 16 cases and best iPhone 15 cases .
